name: kTAF
fix_description: Classic Compound V2 share inflation attack. In exchangeRateStoredInternal, when totalSupply is very small (e.g. 1 wei), an attacker can donate tokens directly to inflate the exchange rate, causing subsequent depositors to mint 0 shares due to integer division truncation. Fix: enforce a minimum initial deposit that mints dead shares, or use virtual shares/assets offset (like OpenZeppelin ERC4626 mitigation).
difficulty_reasoning: This PoC involves a non-obvious lending market exploit with repeated liquidation calculations, cToken collateral seizure constraints, helper-contract orchestration, market entry, borrow/redeem edge cases, and draining protocol liquidity via looping state manipulation. An auditor would need to understand Compound-style internals and protocol-specific accounting across multiple contracts and iterations, which likely takes well over 2 hours to derive from scratch.
